items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I had had the fortune of meeting the guys that made the QRS Little records, the fellows like Lou Louis.

ctx.x: Yes. But I wasn't quite sure whether I played drums or piano because sometimes you'd catch me, I would be playing saxophone. Sometimes I'd be singing. Some places I'd be dancing. Some places I'd get on the show, I'd be doing everything because I remember in 1930 I joined a show and there were 3 pianists. A piano player by the name of Troy and Floyd; Washington, was his last name. That's all I knew because they only called him Washington because in those days they only called, Washington. items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I had a distant cousin that took me back in Chicago and I went to see Mr. Louis Armstrong playing with Erskine Tate at the Vendome Theatre

ctx.x: Normal, Alabama, N-o-r-m-a-l. See because right out from that was the Seventh Day Adventists that later on a lot of peoples joined that. It's Huntsville, J.F. Drake, Alabama, they say, and later on Professor Jack (Tfadrick?) became the Professor. But Mr. James H. Wilson, he had been with the 24th and he had been with the 10th Cavalry and he was a flexible man.
